  ----------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# I. Purpose, Scope and Bottom Line

You asked for a status summary of all closing deliverables ahead of your Wednesday (June 18) call with David Kessler and Priya Nair of Ridgeline and the scheduled Friday, June 20, 2025 Closing Date. We cross-referenced each of the 35 line items (and sub-items) in the June 16 Closing Checklist against (i) the conditions precedent in Section 7.01 and the related collateral, covenant and definitional provisions of the Senior Secured Revolving Credit Agreement dated as of June 13, 2025 (the \"Credit Agreement\" or \"CA\"), (ii) the Officer\'s Compliance Certificate prepared by Sandra Felton (the \"Compliance Certificate\"), and (iii) James Okubo\'s June 16 status email describing deliverables actually received. Capitalized terms have the meanings given in the Credit Agreement.

**Bottom line: we are not in a position to close on June 20 on the current record.** The checklist shows 26 of 35 items as \"Complete,\" but our review identified ten Critical issues --- conditions precedent that are unsatisfied or deliverables that are defective --- several of which the checklist affirmatively mislabels as Complete. The most acute are: (1) no Mortgage, survey or flood determination for the Gastonia Material Real Property; (2) a stale Gastonia Phase I ESA (370 days old against a 180-day requirement); (3) a stale Delaware good standing for Thornfield Distribution Services LLC (63 days old against a 30-day requirement); (4) no Guarantee Agreement and no Virginia UCC-1 for Thornfield Advanced Materials Corp.; (5) no evidence of ESOP Trust (38% member) consent; (6) a Compliance Certificate that omits the Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio; (7) a Lender commitment and signature-page discrepancy for Aldersgate Bank & Trust; (8) a flow of funds built on the \$90,000,000 original Cornerstone principal rather than the \$87,450,000 payoff amount, with no allocation for closing fees; and (9) a Borrowing Request deadline that, because Thursday June 19 (Juneteenth) is not a Business Day, falls at 1:00 p.m. Denver time today, Monday June 16.

Each Critical item can be cured or, failing cure, waived in writing by the Required Lenders (Lenders holding more than 50% of Commitments; Ridgeline alone holds 40.54%, so at least one other Lender must join) under the lead-in to Section 7.01 and Section 13.02. Because the Credit Agreement is held in escrow by the Agent until all Section 7.01 conditions are satisfied or waived (Section 14.01), and terminates if the Closing Date has not occurred by July 31, 2025, any item that cannot be cured by Friday should be raised with Ridgeline on Wednesday as either a waiver/post-closing request or a reason to move the closing.

  **Severity**                        **Meaning**

  **CRITICAL**                        A Section 7.01 condition precedent is unsatisfied, a core Loan Document is missing or defective, or a funding mechanic will fail. Closing cannot occur absent cure or a written Required Lender waiver.

The closing issues memo is written to `/workspace/output/closing-issues-memo.docx`. It passed the docx skill's `validate.py` check and opens cleanly when parsed back. It sorts 28 issues by severity: 10 Critical, 8 High, 5 Moderate and 5 Low. Its conclusion is that the deal cannot close on Friday, June 20, 2025 as things stand. The checklist marks 26 of 35 items "Complete", but at least ten of them should not be.

The Critical issues, each of which blocks closing unless fixed or waived in writing by lenders holding more than 50% of the commitments:
- **Gastonia property:** there is no mortgage, survey or flood hazard determination. Its environmental report (Phase I) is 370 days old, and the agreement allows 180.
- **Thornfield Distribution Services:** its Delaware good standing certificate is 63 days old, and the agreement allows 30. It needs to be reordered now.
- **Thornfield Advanced Materials:** there is no guarantee from it, and no UCC-1 has been filed against it in Virginia.
- **Owner consent:** only Marcus Thornfield (62%) signed the member consent. There is nothing from the ESOP Trust (38%), and nothing addresses ERISA.
- **Compliance certificate:** it leaves out the fixed charge coverage ratio, which the agreement requires. It is also unsigned.
- **Aldersgate Bank & Trust:**
  - The credit agreement gives it a $25M commitment, but the checklist and its note say $35M. The checklist's commitment table therefore adds up to $195M, not $185M.
  - Its signature page is in the name of "Crestview Bank & Trust".
- **Flow of funds:** it sends $90M to Cornerstone, but the payoff letter says $87.45M. It also sets nothing aside for the $6.5M of fees.
- **Borrowing request:** Thursday, June 19 is Juneteenth and not a business day. The three-business-day notice was therefore due by 1:00 p.m. Denver time on Monday, June 16, and the checklist doesn't list it at all.

The memo also gives answers to James Okubo's three open questions, a list of items reviewed without exception, an agenda for Wednesday's call with Ridgeline, and an action plan by responsible party.

The memo relies only on the four documents provided. I did not have the operating agreement, security agreement, title commitments, opinion drafts or other underlying documents, and the memo says so.
